## Introduction  
If you’re looking for a reliable web host that balances price, performance, and ease of use in 2026, a **Hostinger review 2026** is a good place to start. Over the past few years Hostinger has refined its infrastructure, rolled out new data‑center locations, and introduced a refreshed hPanel interface aimed at both beginners and seasoned developers. In this article we’ll walk through the most important aspects — speed, uptime, pricing, features, and support — so you can decide whether Hostinger fits your software projects, blogs, or small business sites.

## Performance Overview  
### Speed & Uptime  
Hostinger’s 2026 network leans heavily on LiteSpeed servers combined with SSD storage and a built‑in caching layer. Independent benchmarks show average page load times around 420 ms for a standard WordPress site hosted on their premium plan, which is competitive with mid‑tier providers. Uptime guarantees sit at 99.9 %, and real‑world monitoring over the last six months recorded an average of 99.94 % availability across their US, EU, and Asia‑Pacific nodes.

### Server Locations  
The company now operates nine data centers: three in the United States (Chicago, Dallas, Seattle), two in Europe (London, Frankfurt), and four in Asia‑Pacific (Singapore, Tokyo, Sydney, Bangalore). This spread lets you pick a location closest to your target audience, reducing latency for users worldwide.

## Pricing Plans  
### Shared Hosting Tiers  
Hostinger offers three shared‑hosting levels: Single, Premium, and Business. The Single plan starts at $1.99 /mo (billed annually) and includes one website, 30 GB SSD storage, and ~10 GB bandwidth. The Premium tier, priced at $2.99 /mo, adds unlimited websites, unlimited bandwidth, and a free SSL certificate. The Business plan at $3.99 /mo throws in daily backups, a free domain for the first year, and enhanced performance resources.

### Cloud & VPS Options  
For software developers needing more control, Hostinger’s cloud hosting begins at $7.99 /mo with dedicated CPU cores and scalable RAM. Their VPS line starts at $4.99 /mo for a basic 1 core/1 GB setup, scaling up to 8 cores/16 GB for $39.99 /mo. All plans include full root access, a choice of operating systems (Ubuntu, CentOS, Debian), and optional managed support add‑ons.

## Key Features  
### Control Panel  
The updated hPanel (replacing the older cPanel‑based interface) provides a clean dashboard with one‑click installers for WordPress, Joomla, Laravel, and Docker containers. File management, DNS editing, and SSL activation are all accessible from the left‑hand navigation pane, making routine tasks quick even for novices.

### Developer Tools  
Hostinger supports PHP 8.2, Node.js 18, Python 3.11, and Ruby 3.2 via Selector. SSH access, Git integration, and Composer are enabled on all paid plans. The platform also offers a built‑in CI/CD pipeline through integration with GitHub Actions, allowing you to push code directly from a repository to a staging environment.

### Security Features  
Free SSL certificates come from Let’s Encrypt on every plan. Advanced security includes ModSecurity web‑application firewall, DDoS mitigation at the network level, and automatic malware scanning. For extra protection, you can upgrade to the SiteLock add‑on, which provides real‑time threat monitoring and automatic cleanup.

## Pros and Cons  
### Advantages  
- Low entry price with generous resource limits  
- Fast LiteSpeed servers and solid uptime  
- Global data‑center network for better
